items.stem:
Nikhil noticed that farmers near Bhopal threw away tonnes of tomatoes when prices fell. He borrowed money, set up a small unit to make tomato puree, hired four workers and sold the puree to hotels. In the first year he made a loss, but he did not give up.
(i) Identify three characteristics of entrepreneurship shown in the case. (ii) Which stages of the entrepreneurial process can you identify?
items.answer: (i) Gap filling or creative response (turning waste into a product); risk bearing (borrowed money, first-year loss); profit potential and purposeful activity (selling to hotels) (any three). (ii) Discovery of an opportunity; resourcing (borrowing, hiring); actualisation (production and sale).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Gap filling or creative response (turning waste into a product); risk bearing (borrowed money, first-year loss); profit potential and purposeful activity (selling to hotels) (any three). (ii) Discovery of an opportunity; resourcing (borrowing, hiring); actualisation (production and sale).

items.answer: The average income per person in an economy.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Every week Harpreet sets sales targets, checks progress and corrects problems in his shop. (a) Which function of the entrepreneur is shown? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.

items.stem: What is meant by "Fear of failure"?
items.answer: The anxiety about losing money or social standing that stops many people from starting a business.
